taboo_mechanism: Do not look backward until crossing completely into upper sunlight; Orpheus sings to guide the soul back.
outcome_of_glance: Eurydice vanishes back to Hades; Orpheus later suffers dismemberment (sparagmos) and his head prophesies on Lesbos.
anthropologist_or_scholar: E.R. Dodds (The Greeks and the Irrational) & Karl Meuli / Mircea Eliade
structural_meaning: Interprets Orpheus as an archaic northern shaman/soul-guide whose ecstatic song retrieves lost souls from the spirit world, later fused with Dionysiac initiatory death-and-rebirth.

tradition_or_myth: Kojiki (712 CE) & Nihon Shoki: Descent into Yomi
taboo_mechanism: Izanami forbids Izanagi from looking at her while she petitions the gods of Yomi (Land of Gloom) to return.
outcome_of_glance: Izanagi lights a tooth of his hair-comb, sees Izanami's rotting, maggot-ridden corpse; terrified, he flees as she seals the border with a boulder, creating permanent human mortality.
structural_meaning: Explains the origin of death's irreversibility and why living ritualists must purify themselves (misogi) after contact with the dead.

taboo_mechanism: 'Flee for your life! Do not look behind you, nor stop anywhere in the plain.'
outcome_of_glance: Lot's wife looks back behind him and is instantly transformed into a pillar of salt.
anthropologist_or_scholar: Sir James Frazer & Folklore Motif-Index C331 / C961.1
structural_meaning: Marks the sacred boundary between judgment/destruction and deliverance; looking back breaks ritual separation from a doomed order.

figures: Bereaved Husband & Deceased Wife in the Ghost Land
taboo_mechanism: A mourning husband tracks his wife's soul across a shaking bridge to the Land of the Dead, wins permission to carry her back in a basket or beside him, but must NOT touch, sleep, or look at her for four days/nights.
outcome_of_glance: On the final night just before dawn/home, impatience or touch breaks the rule and the wife returns permanently to the ghost village as a dry bone or shadow.
anthropologist_or_scholar: Åke Hultkrantz (The North American Indian Orpheus Tradition, 1957 — cataloging ~130 variants)
structural_meaning: Hultkrantz proved these stories arose independently from indigenous shamanic soul-recovery practices and funeral taboos teaching communities to accept death's finality.

tradition_or_myth: The Daughter of the Sun (Cherokee Orpheus Myth)
taboo_mechanism: Seven messengers travel to the Darkening Land in the west to retrieve the Sun's daughter inside a closed box—strictly forbidden to open the lid until reaching home.
outcome_of_glance: As she begs for air near the end of the journey, they crack the lid slightly to look/soothe her; a redbird (cardinal) flies out and the Sun's daughter is lost.
structural_meaning: Combines the Orpheus motif with an etiological myth explaining why human death cannot be reversed and how the redbird received its color.

taboo_mechanism: Hiku descends into Milu (the underworld) on a vine swing smeared with foul smell so ghosts mistake him for dead, catches Kawelu's butterfly-spirit in a coconut shell, and restores her—without premature opening.
outcome_of_glance: In most Hawaiian versions, Hiku SUCCEEDS because he keeps the ritual seal intact until returning her spirit upward through her feet!
structural_meaning: Demonstrates an optimistic Polynesian counterpart where strict observance of ritual containment triumphs over death.

taboo_mechanism: After mistreating his spirit-wife Niwareka, Mataora descends to Rarohenga, repents, receives true permanent facial tattooing (tā moko), and earns her return on condition of leaving behind the underworld cloak/customs respectfully.
outcome_of_glance: Niwareka returns safely with Mataora to the upper world, bringing the sacred arts of tattooing and weaving.
anthropologist_or_scholar: Elsdon Best & Te Rangi Hīroa (Sir Peter Buck)
structural_meaning: Here the underworld journey is a rite of moral transformation and craft-initiation rather than tragic failure.

culture_or_region: North America (Great Lakes / Northeast — Huron-Wendat & Blackfoot)
taboo_mechanism: The traveler must endure trials (crossing a narrow log over raging water while a guard dog barks) and obey silence/unopened-bundle taboos on the return road.
outcome_of_glance: Breaking the boundary rule dissolves the revived body back into smoke or compels the mourner to surrender grief.
structural_meaning: Maps seasonal grief rituals and community boundaries between the living hearth and ancestral spirit world.
